questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibility of studying at a good and internationally well-recognized as well as historical university made me choose Paris as my study destination with the opportunity of studying at Sorbonne Université. Further, I wanted to experience the French hospital system and understand the differences and similarities of being a doctor in France compared to in Denmark. Also, I had heard about the hospitals, where I had my internships, and I wanted to get the experience of working there as part of my education. I have lived in and have a personal connection to Paris, so I also wanted to establish an academic and career connection to Paris as well as get the experience of studying here.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I received all the information that I needed to know upon arrival. I arrived some weeks in advance, so I had time to get the initial signatures as well as coordinate the last documents that I needed to handle in Paris, such as Bank information and the establishment of my account in the French hospital system. I received the address of the International Office of Sorbonne Université as well as the location and mails for the responsible doctors of the hospitals, and I was told to write to them a week in advance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive a special assistance. I arrived myself, I knew the city well before my arrival, and then I contacted the university and did most of the administrative parts by mail. Luckily, we were two students that arrived in the same semester, so we could talk to and guide each other about the administrative parts as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I do not have any specific recommendations. I found my apartment through friends from the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Personally, I prefer living off campus. If you don't know the city well and have a hard time with the language, maybe it can be easier to live on-campus and be with other students. Perhaps this is also the case if you want to be sure to have a social circle. Personally, I prefer living in my own apartment inside the city and not as part of an international student environment, and I had a great time living off campus or outside a student environment. It can be difficult to find a place in the city if you don't know the city and places beforehand, and the student houses can therefore oftentimes be more efficient and easy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I believe the International Student's Area have housing opportunities for international exchange student. Besides this, I did not remember that the university itself offered specific housing. Also, finding an apartment in the city is oftentimes difficult if you don't know places yourself.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After being selected by our own university, we received a mail from Sorbonne Université with all the information that we needed to upload and information about the process to follow. There was a specific web-side, where we could follow what we needed to do and upload the documents step by step. I found it very intuitive and the deadlines were clear. There were multiple documents to upload and letters to write, but it was manageable. Closer to the internship start, we had to upload information about our address, bank and transport, which could be difficult to deliver before arrival. In the same time, we had to do a separate file to get the access to the French hospital system.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Office of Sorbonne Université answered fast and well to e-mails through the whole process. Also, we could write to our own university, Københavns Universitet.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The registration went well and I got the two internships that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice would be to make an overview of all the documents and information that need to be delivered and when they should be delivered. Make a timeline. Also, start finding housing in good time if it is possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wanted to participate more with the older doctors at the level of consultations, but I had duties as a student and had to talk with the patients at the hospital daily. I was happy that we had educational hours each week at the hospital at both internships. I had to find the information of the evening lectures myself through the other students, also since they were not obligatory or part of our stay.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was primarily traineeship at the hospitals. It was expected that we had an academic background knowledge on the diseases of the department, which we also had, and that we were able to do somatic clinical as well as neurological examinations of the patients. Also, we did weekly presentations of the patients and were asked academic questions as well on symptoms, diseases and treatment as well. I participated as the other French students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At the traineeships, we have more responsibility at Sorbonne than at UCPH, we have patients that we see typically each day, depending on the department/service, and we also, typically, have to make weekly presentations as well with the senior doctors, which we do not do as regularly at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Traineeship in Pediatrics at Hôpital Armand Trousseau and in Psychiatry at Hôpital de la Pitié Salpêtrière.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend that future exchange students chose traineeships in the fields that they are interested in. It is nice to experience multiple hospitals.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs, but since you are not in your usual environment with known schedules or routines, you tend to buy more outside.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: A bigger part of the transport was refunded, so that was less expensive than I expected. Food is more or less the same as in Denmark, or it is cheaper, but more is bought outside. Apartment rent is more expensive here.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use clubs and sports, but I used the university areas as well as all the libraries that were available and I enjoyed it very much. Also, students engage a lot in Paris with student activities also regarding society, and I received mails and invitations to events like these for students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The host university organized non-academic lectures on different topics for students, and students organized social and cultural events together. I did not know of or wanted to participate in athletic activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I personally liked the broad non-academic lectures for students. Also, Paris is a great city with a lot of things to do outside the area of the host university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Paris has a lot of great areas, parks, museums - you will not be bored.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: To me, it was very easy and natural to adjust to the local culture of my exchange site.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk with fellow students at the university, read at the libraries and participate in lectures.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging. I enjoyed the culture. We arrive later in the morning, have a long lunch break, and the doctors, as well as other fields, stay longer. You must remember to respect the elder.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate the formalities in the culture. I appreciate the time schedule of the day, the multicultural and international environment, the academic level at Sorbonne Université, the atmosphere of a metropol capital.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
First, I would say that it helps a lot if you are able to speak French, not perfectly or necessarily fluently, but that you practice before you arrive and are prepared that the hospitals and doctors will typically expect that you do things more or less on your own as well as with other students. Your French will get better at your stay, but you have to be allright with trying to speak French even though it might be difficult and not at all perfect. The language barrier is what can make it more difficult to participate. 
Secondly, try to ask the doctors if you want to see or do something specific. 
Thirdly, organize your papers and documents, so you know when and what to upload and deliver.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, I would mostly say that the language should be a first priority. Engage with people around you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part must have been being a student at Sorbonne Université, education at the hospitals, lectures at the university. Long time of clinical rotation with the specialties that you like and it gives good experience within the fields (these clinical electives are longer than any rotations we have in Denmark)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge must have been the language barrier. You need to adjust to a new place and environment, do your job and work as well as doing it in a language you are not used to using professionally.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
